Subject: Follow-up: logging & redaction requirements (post-call)

Marcus — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so we can scope a PoC.

High-level requirements (prioritized):
- Remove or pseudonymize direct identifiers from both request and response payloads (names, SSNs, email addresses).
- Suppress or mask sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Session-*).
- Ensure trace identifiers (trace_id / span_id) are either removed or deterministically pseudonymized so we can correlate events without exposing original IDs.
- Per-tenant retention controls: we need configurable retention windows (30 / 90 / 365 / 2555 days for legal hold).
- Data residency: logs must remain in us-east-1 for the production cluster.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence and a standard BAA for HIPAA workloads — please confirm availability.

Attached is a small sample of raw request/response fragments (carebridge-sample-raw-logs.json) — it contains synthetic PHI but mirrors our production shape. Can your team produce a sample scrubbed output and a short note on the approach (regex vs structured parse, hashing scheme for IDs, whether masking is reversible)?

Also: what is the expected timeline for a sandbox PoC (scrubbed logs + live demo)? Tom and I prefer the week of Oct 25th.

Thanks,
Sara

Sara — really helpful list, thanks for sending the sample. Short post-call recap + proposed next steps below.

Recap (what we heard)
- Full request/response sanitization required, with deterministic pseudonyms for patient_id so you can re-identify within your environment if needed.
- Header suppression for Authorization/Cookie + configurable header allowlist.
- Trace IDs: you want correlation without raw IDs leaving logs — deterministic hashing or tokenization are both options.
- Per-tenant retention windows + legal-hold override.
- Residency: us-east-1 only for production audit logs.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report; BAA available via our legal team.

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline)
1) Engineering feasibility + sample scrub: Neha will take the sample JSON and produce a side-by-side scrubbed example (PDF + scrubbed JSON). Target: Oct 27. (owner: neha_kapoor)
2) Technical deep-dive / PoC call (demo of scrub + retention controls): 30 minutes. Proposed slots: Oct 26–28. Marcus to confirm availability and calendar invite. (owner: marcus_lin)
3) Compliance packet & BAA: I’ll loop in legal; expect an initial packet within 3 business days. (owner: marcus_lin)
4) Decision criteria call: after PoC you want an evaluation checklist (sanitization coverage, performance impact, auditability). We’ll provide a short rubric. Target: Nov 3.

Quick technical notes so expectations align:
- Scrubbing approaches: we typically combine structured parsing (when payload schema is available) with regex fallback. Deterministic pseudonymization uses keyed HMAC with a tenant-specific salt — this keeps IDs stable but non-reversible without the salt. We’ll document options for reversible tokenization if you need re-identification under strict controls.
- Headers: we support allowlists/deny-lists per route; Authorization and Cookie are deny-by-default in our recommended configuration.
- Retention: per-tenant retention is configurable at the route level in Redwood Dedicated/Private; hosted plans can be scoped for specific retention buckets.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the PoC/demo. If the Oct 26–28 window works for you, reply with preferred times and timezone (PDT assumed).

Best,
Marcus

Thanks, Marcus — Oct 26 or 27 both work. A couple clarifications to help Neha’s work:
- The sample attached contains a field patient_id that must be pseudonymized deterministically (same patient_id -> same pseudonym across events). Reversible tokenization is acceptable only if the token store is under our control.
- We occasionally surface limited PHI in response bodies (diagnosis codes, partial zip); those need to be scrubbed or generalized (e.g., ZIP -> 3-digit or region).
- For legal hold: we may need to preserve full events for up to 7 years for flagged records, but retention for analytics can be much shorter. Implementation should include a legal-hold flag.

I’ve attached a short doc outlining HIPAA scope for our logs (carebridge-hipaa-scope.docx). Please treat it as sensitive.
